(No details on establishment) || Unknown || Southern Shinano Province || However, other documents mention {{ill|Shinano Province|ja|科野国|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano Province|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 科野国造}} as having the {{ill|Shinano (Shinano no Kuni) Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|科野国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano (Shinano no Kuni) Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}}. Hayagoeue-no-mikoto is the progenitor of the Iyo Kuni no Miyatsuko. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shinano Province|Shinano Province]] | '''{{ill|Suwa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|洲羽国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|qq=}}''' || すわ || {{ill|Take Ōomi no mikoto|ja|建大臣命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Take Ōomi no mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武国彦命}}
[[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] || Unknown || Central Shinano Province || In the “[[:en:Kujiki|Sendai Kuji Hongi (Kujihongi)]]” Kuni no Miyatsuko Honki, the mention of a Kuni no Miyatsuko in Suwa is believed to be an error for {{ill|Nasu Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|那須国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nasu Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}}. All details such as the appointment period, the founding ancestor Take Ōomi no mikoto, or how it was established, come from the forged texts “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” “Aso Family Brief Genealogy,” “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” and “Various Genealogies,” so it is considered certain to be a fictional Kuni no Miyatsuko.Ryōtarō Maeda, “Reconsidering the ‘Shinshi Keizu’ in the ‘Ōhori-bon’ & ‘Aso-ke ryaku keifu’: Reconstructed Suwa Traditions,” in “Studies in Japanese Language and Literature” No.161, August 2023. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shinano Province|Shinano Province]] | '''{{ill|Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|木蘇国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|qq=}}''' || きそ || Ototekehiko-no-mikoto
(No details on establishment) || Unknown || Southern Shinano Province || References to Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko appear only in the forged “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” “Aso Family Brief Genealogy,” “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” “Various Genealogies,” etc., so it is regarded as certainly fictional.Ryōtarō Maeda, “Reconsidering the ‘Shinshi Keizu’ in the ‘Ōhori-bon’ & ‘Aso-ke ryaku keifu’: Reconstructed Suwa Traditions,” in “Studies in Japanese Language and Literature” No.161, August 2023. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:San'yōdō|Sanyōdō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Aki Province|Aki Province]] | '''{{ill|Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|沼田国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|qq=}}''' || ぬた || {{ill|Akinosayatama no mikoto|ja|飽速玉命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akinosayatama no mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} || The Tsukushi clan || Eastern Aki Province || The priestly family of {{ill|Numata Shrine|ja|沼田神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Numata Shrine|qq=}} claims descent from the Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko. Akinosayatama no mikoto is the progenitor of the Aki Kuni no Miyatsuko. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:San'indō|San'indō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Izumo Province|Izumo Province]] | '''{{ill|Susa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|須佐国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || すさ || Bon-nari

Seihen,” “Various Genealogies,” etc., so it is regarded as certainly fictional.Ryōtarō Maeda, “Reconsidering the ‘Shinshi Keizu’ in the ‘Ōhori-bon’ & ‘Aso-ke ryaku keifu’: Reconstructed Suwa Traditions,” in “Studies in Japanese Language and Literature” No.161, August 2023. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:San'yōdō|Sanyōdō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Aki Province|Aki Province]] | '''{{ill|Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|沼田国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|qq=}}''' || ぬた || {{ill|Akinosayatama no mikoto|ja|飽速玉命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akinosayatama no mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} || The Tsukushi clan || Eastern Aki Province || The priestly family of {{ill|Numata Shrine|ja|沼田神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Numata Shrine|qq=}} claims descent from the Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko. (Possibly during Jingo Keiun 1 [767 CE]) || The Dōshima clan (Sukune) || Mutsu Province || Created by merging the various Mutsu Kuni no Miyatsuko. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Dewa Province|Dewa Province]] | '''{{ill|Dewa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|出羽国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dewa Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || でわ || (Wadō 5 [712 CE]) || Unknown || Dewa Province || Split off from Mutsu Province and Echigo Province. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:San'indō|San'indō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Mimasaka Province|Mimasaka Province]] | '''{{ill|Mimasaka Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|美作国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimasaka Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || みまさか || (Wadō 6 [713 CE]) || Unknown || Mimasaka Province || Split off from Bizen Province. |} {{-}} === Kuni no Miyatsuko Deemed Not to Have Existed === The following Kuni no Miyatsuko appear in shrine traditions, in the “Suwa Historical Materials” Volume 28 (the “Suwa Shimo-sha Ōhori (Ohoribe) Takei Iwai Kei Zu Ryaku”), or in what are considered forged texts such as the “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” the “{{ill|Aso Family Brief Genealogy|ja|阿蘇家略系図|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aso Family Brief Genealogy|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}},” the “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” “Various Genealogies,” etc. Since these are of low credibility and do not appear in other reliable sources, it is believed these Kuni no Miyatsuko did not actually exist. {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;font-size:85%" align="left" !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Ritsuryō Province !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" colspan="2" | Name of Kuni no Miyatsuko !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | First Kuni no Miyatsuko
(Period of Appointment) !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Clan (the bracketed term is [[:en:Kabane|Kabane]]) !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Domain !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Notes |- !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" | Notation !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" | Reading |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:Tōkaidō (region)|Tōkaidō (region)]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] | '''{{ill|Shimada Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|嶋田国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimada Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'''
(Owari no Kuni Shimada Kuni no Miyatsuko) || しまだ || Nakaotomi no Koage
(No details on establishment) || Possibly the Shimada clan? (Omuraji) || Southern Owari Province || Possibly linked to the Shimada Omuraji of the Ta clan. Nakaotomi no Koage is said to be the ancestor of the Niwa Agatanushi. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shimōsa Province|Shimōsa Province]] | '''{{ill|Fusa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|布佐国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fusa Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || ふさ || {{ill|Ame no Tomi no mikoto|ja|天富命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Tomi no mikoto|qq=}}
(Emperor Jinmu period) || The Imbe (Inbe) clan (Kubi) || Western Shimōsa Province || According to the tradition of {{ill|Takeuchi Shrine (Hyōgo)|ja|竹内神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeuchi Shrine (Hyōgo)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 竹内神社 (我孫子市)}}. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:Tōsandō|Tōsandō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shinano Province|Shinano Province]] | '''{{ill|Ina Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|伊奈国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ina Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || いな || Hayagoeue-no-mikoto
(No details on establishment) || Unknown || Southern Shinano Province || However, other documents mention {{ill|Shinano Province|ja|科野国|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano Province|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 科野国造}} as having the {{ill|Shinano (Shinano no Kuni) Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|科野国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano (Shinano no Kuni) Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}}. Hayagoeue-no-mikoto is the progenitor of the Iyo Kuni no Miyatsuko. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shinano Province|Shinano Province]] | '''{{ill|Suwa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|洲羽国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|qq=}}''' || すわ || {{ill|Take Ōomi no mikoto|ja|建大臣命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Take Ōomi no mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武国彦命}}
[[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] || Unknown || Central Shinano Province || In the “[[:en:Kujiki|Sendai Kuji Hongi (Kujihongi)]]” Kuni no Miyatsuko Honki, the mention of a Kuni no Miyatsuko in Suwa is believed to be an error for {{ill|Nasu Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|那須国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nasu Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}}. All details such as the appointment period, the founding ancestor Take Ōomi no mikoto, or how it was established, come from the forged texts “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” “Aso Family Brief Genealogy,” “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” and “Various Genealogies,” so it is considered certain to be a fictional Kuni no Miyatsuko.Ryōtarō Maeda, “Reconsidering the ‘Shinshi Keizu’ in the ‘Ōhori-bon’ & ‘Aso-ke ryaku keifu’: Reconstructed Suwa Traditions,” in “Studies in Japanese Language and Literature” No.161, August 2023. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shinano Province|Shinano Province]] | '''{{ill|Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|木蘇国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|qq=}}''' || きそ || Ototekehiko-no-mikoto
(No details on establishment) || Unknown || Southern Shinano Province || References to Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko appear only in the forged “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” “Aso Family Brief Genealogy,” “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” “Various Genealogies,” etc., so it is regarded as certainly fictional.Ryōtarō Maeda, “Reconsidering the ‘Shinshi Keizu’ in the ‘Ōhori-bon’ & ‘Aso-ke ryaku keifu’: Reconstructed Suwa Traditions,” in “Studies in Japanese Language and Literature” No.161, August 2023. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:San'yōdō|Sanyōdō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Aki Province|Aki Province]] | '''{{ill|Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|沼田国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|qq=}}''' || ぬた || {{ill|Akinosayatama no mikoto|ja|飽速玉命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akinosayatama no mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} || The Tsukushi clan || Eastern Aki Province || The priestly family of {{ill|Numata Shrine|ja|沼田神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Numata Shrine|qq=}} claims descent from the Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko. Akinosayatama no mikoto is the progenitor of the Aki Kuni no Miyatsuko. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:San'indō|San'indō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Izumo Province|Izumo Province]] | '''{{ill|Susa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|須佐国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || すさ || Bon-nari

Seihen,” “Various Genealogies,” etc. Since these are of low credibility and do not appear in other reliable sources, it is believed these Kuni no Miyatsuko did not actually exist. {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;font-size:85%" align="left" !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Ritsuryō Province !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" colspan="2" | Name of Kuni no Miyatsuko !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | First Kuni no Miyatsuko
(Period of Appointment) !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Clan (the bracketed term is [[:en:Kabane|Kabane]]) !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Domain !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Notes |- !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" | Notation !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" | Reading |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:Tōkaidō (region)|Tōkaidō (region)]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] | '''{{ill|Shimada Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|嶋田国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimada Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'''
(Owari no Kuni Shimada Kuni no Miyatsuko) || しまだ || Nakaotomi no Koage
(No details on establishment) || Possibly the Shimada clan? (Omuraji) || Southern Owari Province || Possibly linked to the Shimada Omuraji of the Ta clan. Nakaotomi no Koage is said to be the ancestor of the Niwa Agatanushi. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shimōsa Province|Shimōsa Province]] | '''{{ill|Fusa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|布佐国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fusa Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || ふさ || {{ill|Ame no Tomi no mikoto|ja|天富命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Tomi no mikoto|qq=}}
(Emperor Jinmu period) || The Imbe (Inbe) clan (Kubi) || Western Shimōsa Province || According to the tradition of {{ill|Takeuchi Shrine (Hyōgo)|ja|竹内神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeuchi Shrine (Hyōgo)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 竹内神社 (我孫子市)}}. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:Tōsandō|Tōsandō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shinano Province|Shinano Province]] | '''{{ill|Ina Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|伊奈国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ina Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || いな || Hayagoeue-no-mikoto
(No details on establishment) || Unknown || Southern Shinano Province || However, other documents mention {{ill|Shinano Province|ja|科野国|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano Province|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 科野国造}} as having the {{ill|Shinano (Shinano no Kuni) Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|科野国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano (Shinano no Kuni) Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}}. Hayagoeue-no-mikoto is the progenitor of the Iyo Kuni no Miyatsuko. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shinano Province|Shinano Province]] | '''{{ill|Suwa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|洲羽国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|qq=}}''' || すわ || {{ill|Take Ōomi no mikoto|ja|建大臣命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Take Ōomi no mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武国彦命}}
[[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] || Unknown || Central Shinano Province || In the “[[:en:Kujiki|Sendai Kuji Hongi (Kujihongi)]]” Kuni no Miyatsuko Honki, the mention of a Kuni no Miyatsuko in Suwa is believed to be an error for {{ill|Nasu Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|那須国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nasu Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}}. All details such as the appointment period, the founding ancestor Take Ōomi no mikoto, or how it was established, come from the forged texts “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” “Aso Family Brief Genealogy,” “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” and “Various Genealogies,” so it is considered certain to be a fictional Kuni no Miyatsuko.Ryōtarō Maeda, “Reconsidering the ‘Shinshi Keizu’ in the ‘Ōhori-bon’ & ‘Aso-ke ryaku keifu’: Reconstructed Suwa Traditions,” in “Studies in Japanese Language and Literature” No.161, August 2023. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shinano Province|Shinano Province]] | '''{{ill|Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|木蘇国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|qq=}}''' || きそ || Ototekehiko-no-mikoto
(No details on establishment) || Unknown || Southern Shinano Province || References to Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko appear only in the forged “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” “Aso Family Brief Genealogy,” “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” “Various Genealogies,” etc., so it is regarded as certainly fictional.Ryōtarō Maeda, “Reconsidering the ‘Shinshi Keizu’ in the ‘Ōhori-bon’ & ‘Aso-ke ryaku keifu’: Reconstructed Suwa Traditions,” in “Studies in Japanese Language and Literature” No.161, August 2023. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:San'yōdō|Sanyōdō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Aki Province|Aki Province]] | '''{{ill|Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|沼田国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|qq=}}''' || ぬた || {{ill|Akinosayatama no mikoto|ja|飽速玉命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akinosayatama no mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} || The Tsukushi clan || Eastern Aki Province || The priestly family of {{ill|Numata Shrine|ja|沼田神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Numata Shrine|qq=}} claims descent from the Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko. Akinosayatama no mikoto is the progenitor of the Aki Kuni no Miyatsuko. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:San'indō|San'indō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Izumo Province|Izumo Province]] | '''{{ill|Susa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|須佐国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || すさ || Bon-nari
(Emperor Seimu period) || The Susa clan || Southwestern Izumo Province || The priestly family of {{ill|Susa Shrine (Shimane)|ja|須佐神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susa Shrine (Shimane)|qq=}} claims descent from the Susa Kuni no Miyatsuko. |} {{-}} '''Kuni no Miyatsuko Ichiran''' (国造一覧) {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 1]] }} [[ja:国造]] [[sn:List of Kuni no Miyatsuko]] [[ja:国造一覧]] [[sn: failed]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]] [[Category:Kofun period]] [[Category:Kuni no miyatsuko]] [[Category:Titles and Positions in Shintō]] [[Category:Asuka period]] [[en:Kuni no miyatsuko]] [[es:Kuni no miyatsuko]] [[it:Kuni no miyatsuko]] [[ko:국조 (일본)]] [[simple:Kuni no miyatsuko]] [[vi:Kuni no miyatsuko]] [[zh:國造]]

Seihen,” “Various Genealogies,” etc. Since these are of low credibility and do not appear in other reliable sources, it is believed these Kuni no Miyatsuko did not actually exist. {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;font-size:85%" align="left" !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Ritsuryō Province !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" colspan="2" | Name of Kuni no Miyatsuko !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | First Kuni no Miyatsuko
(Period of Appointment) !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Clan (the bracketed term is [[:en:Kabane|Kabane]]) !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Domain !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Notes |- !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" | Notation !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" | Reading |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:Tōkaidō (region)|Tōkaidō (region)]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] | '''{{ill|Shimada Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|嶋田国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimada Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'''
(Owari no Kuni Shimada Kuni no Miyatsuko) || しまだ || Nakaotomi no Koage
(No details on establishment) || Possibly the Shimada clan? (Omuraji) || Southern Owari Province || Possibly linked to the Shimada Omuraji of the Ta clan. Nakaotomi no Koage is said to be the ancestor of the Niwa Agatanushi. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shimōsa Province|Shimōsa Province]] | '''{{ill|Fusa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|布佐国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fusa Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || ふさ || {{ill|Ame no Tomi no mikoto|ja|天富命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Tomi no mikoto|qq=|1=Ame-no-Tomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q24899653}}
(Emperor Jinmu period) || The Imbe (Inbe) clan (Kubi) || Western Shimōsa Province || According to the tradition of {{ill|Takeuchi Shrine (Hyōgo)|ja|竹内神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeuchi Shrine (Hyōgo)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 竹内神社 (我孫子市)|1=Takeuchi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q97218316}}. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:Tōsandō|Tōsandō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shinano Province|Shinano Province]] | '''{{ill|Ina Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|伊奈国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ina Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || いな || Hayagoeue-no-mikoto
(No details on establishment) || Unknown || Southern Shinano Province || However, other documents mention {{ill|Shinano Province|ja|科野国|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano Province|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 科野国造|1=Shinano no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11595951}} as having the {{ill|Shinano (Shinano no Kuni) Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|科野国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano (Shinano no Kuni) Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=|1=Shinano no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11595951}}. Hayagoeue-no-mikoto is the progenitor of the Iyo Kuni no Miyatsuko. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shinano Province|Shinano Province]] | '''{{ill|Suwa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|洲羽国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|qq=|1=Suwa-no-kokuzo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q67499361}}''' || すわ || {{ill|Take Ōomi no mikoto|ja|建大臣命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Take Ōomi no mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武国彦命|1=Takakuni no Hikono Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q100453594}}
[[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] || Unknown || Central Shinano Province || In the “[[:en:Kujiki|Sendai Kuji Hongi (Kujihongi)]]” Kuni no Miyatsuko Honki, the mention of a Kuni no Miyatsuko in Suwa is believed to be an error for {{ill|Nasu Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|那須国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nasu Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=|1=Nasu no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11642909}}. All details such as the appointment period, the founding ancestor Take Ōomi no mikoto, or how it was established, come from the forged texts “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” “Aso Family Brief Genealogy,” “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” and “Various Genealogies,” so it is considered certain to be a fictional Kuni no Miyatsuko.Ryōtarō Maeda, “Reconsidering the ‘Shinshi Keizu’ in the ‘Ōhori-bon’ & ‘Aso-ke ryaku keifu’: Reconstructed Suwa Traditions,” in “Studies in Japanese Language and Literature” No.161, August 2023. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shinano Province|Shinano Province]] | '''{{ill|Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|木蘇国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|qq=|1=Kiso no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q85881055}}''' || きそ || Ototekehiko-no-mikoto
(No details on establishment) || Unknown || Southern Shinano Province || References to Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko appear only in the forged “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” “Aso Family Brief Genealogy,” “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” “Various Genealogies,” etc., so it is regarded as certainly fictional.Ryōtarō Maeda, “Reconsidering the ‘Shinshi Keizu’ in the ‘Ōhori-bon’ & ‘Aso-ke ryaku keifu’: Reconstructed Suwa Traditions,” in “Studies in Japanese Language and Literature” No.161, August 2023. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:San'yōdō|Sanyōdō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Aki Province|Aki Province]] | '''{{ill|Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|沼田国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|qq=|1=Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11554571}}''' || ぬた || {{ill|Akinosayatama no mikoto|ja|飽速玉命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akinosayatama no mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} || The Tsukushi clan || Eastern Aki Province || The priestly family of {{ill|Numata Shrine|ja|沼田神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Numata Shrine|qq=|1=Numata Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11554607}} claims descent from the Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko. Akinosayatama no mikoto is the progenitor of the Aki Kuni no Miyatsuko. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:San'indō|San'indō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Izumo Province|Izumo Province]] | '''{{ill|Susa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|須佐国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || すさ || Bon-nari
(Emperor Seimu period) || The Susa clan || Southwestern Izumo Province || The priestly family of {{ill|Susa Shrine (Shimane)|ja|須佐神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susa Shrine (Shimane)|qq=|1=Susa Shrine (Shimane)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11664499}} claims descent from the Susa Kuni no Miyatsuko. |} {{-}} '''Kuni no Miyatsuko Ichiran''' (国造一覧) {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 1]] }} [[ja:国造]] [[sn:List of Kuni no Miyatsuko]] [[ja:国造一覧]] [[sn: failed]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]] [[Category:Kofun period]] [[Category:Kuni no miyatsuko]] [[Category:Titles and Positions in Shintō]] [[Category:Asuka period]] [[en:Kuni no miyatsuko]] [[es:Kuni no miyatsuko]] [[it:Kuni no miyatsuko]] [[ko:국조 (일본)]] [[simple:Kuni no miyatsuko]] [[vi:Kuni no miyatsuko]] [[zh:國造]]

Seihen,” “Various Genealogies,” etc. Since these are of low credibility and do not appear in other reliable sources, it is believed these Kuni no Miyatsuko did not actually exist. {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;font-size:85%" align="left" !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Ritsuryō Province !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" colspan="2" | Name of Kuni no Miyatsuko !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | First Kuni no Miyatsuko
(Period of Appointment) !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Clan (the bracketed term is [[:en:Kabane|Kabane]]) !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Domain !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Notes |- !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" | Notation !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" | Reading |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:Tōkaidō (region)|Tōkaidō (region)]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] | '''{{ill|Shimada Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|嶋田国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimada Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'''
(Owari no Kuni Shimada Kuni no Miyatsuko) || しまだ || Nakaotomi no Koage
(No details on establishment) || Possibly the Shimada clan? (Omuraji) || Southern Owari Province || Possibly linked to the Shimada Omuraji of the Ta clan. Nakaotomi no Koage is said to be the ancestor of the Niwa Agatanushi. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shimōsa Province|Shimōsa Province]] | '''{{ill|Fusa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|布佐国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fusa Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || ふさ || {{ill|Ame no Tomi no mikoto|ja|天富命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Tomi no mikoto|qq=|1=Ame-no-Tomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q24899653}}
(Emperor Jinmu period) || The Imbe (Inbe) clan (Kubi) || Western Shimōsa Province || According to the tradition of {{ill|Takeuchi Shrine (Hyōgo)|ja|竹内神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeuchi Shrine (Hyōgo)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 竹内神社 (我孫子市)|1=Takeuchi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q97218316}}. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:Tōsandō|Tōsandō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shinano Province|Shinano Province]] | '''{{ill|Ina Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|伊奈国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ina Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || いな || Hayagoeue-no-mikoto
(No details on establishment) || Unknown || Southern Shinano Province || However, other documents mention {{ill|Shinano Province|ja|科野国|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano Province|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 科野国造|1=Shinano no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11595951}} as having the {{ill|Shinano (Shinano no Kuni) Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|科野国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano (Shinano no Kuni) Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=|1=Shinano no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11595951}}. Hayagoeue-no-mikoto is the progenitor of the Iyo Kuni no Miyatsuko. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shinano Province|Shinano Province]] | '''{{ill|Suwa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|洲羽国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|qq=|1=Suwa-no-kokuzo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q67499361}}''' || すわ || {{ill|Take Ōomi no mikoto|ja|建大臣命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Take Ōomi no mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武国彦命|1=Takakuni no Hikono Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q100453594}}
[[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] || Unknown || Central Shinano Province || In the “[[:en:Kujiki|Sendai Kuji Hongi (Kujihongi)]]” Kuni no Miyatsuko Honki, the mention of a Kuni no Miyatsuko in Suwa is believed to be an error for {{ill|Nasu Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|那須国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nasu Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=|1=Nasu no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11642909}}. All details such as the appointment period, the founding ancestor Take Ōomi no mikoto, or how it was established, come from the forged texts “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” “Aso Family Brief Genealogy,” “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” and “Various Genealogies,” so it is considered certain to be a fictional Kuni no Miyatsuko.Ryōtarō Maeda, “Reconsidering the ‘Shinshi Keizu’ in the ‘Ōhori-bon’ & ‘Aso-ke ryaku keifu’: Reconstructed Suwa Traditions,” in “Studies in Japanese Language and Literature” No.161, August 2023. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shinano Province|Shinano Province]] | '''{{ill|Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|木蘇国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|qq=|1=Kiso no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q85881055}}''' || きそ || Ototekehiko-no-mikoto
(No details on establishment) || Unknown || Southern Shinano Province || References to Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko appear only in the forged “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” “Aso Family Brief Genealogy,” “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” “Various Genealogies,” etc., so it is regarded as certainly fictional.Ryōtarō Maeda, “Reconsidering the ‘Shinshi Keizu’ in the ‘Ōhori-bon’ & ‘Aso-ke ryaku keifu’: Reconstructed Suwa Traditions,” in “Studies in Japanese Language and Literature” No.161, August 2023. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:San'yōdō|Sanyōdō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Aki Province|Aki Province]] | '''{{ill|Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|沼田国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|qq=|1=Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11554571}}''' || ぬた || {{ill|Akinosayatama no mikoto|ja|飽速玉命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akinosayatama no mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} || The Tsukushi clan || Eastern Aki Province || The priestly family of {{ill|Numata Shrine|ja|沼田神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Numata Shrine|qq=|1=Numata Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11554607}} claims descent from the Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko. Akinosayatama no mikoto is the progenitor of the Aki Kuni no Miyatsuko. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:San'indō|San'indō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Izumo Province|Izumo Province]] | '''{{ill|Susa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|須佐国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || すさ || Bon-nari
(Emperor Seimu period) || The Susa clan || Southwestern Izumo Province || The priestly family of {{ill|Susa Shrine (Shimane)|ja|須佐神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susa Shrine (Shimane)|qq=|1=Susa Shrine (Shimane)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11664499}} claims descent from the Susa Kuni no Miyatsuko. |} {{-}} '''Kuni no Miyatsuko Ichiran''' (国造一覧) {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 1]] }} [[ja:国造]] [[sn:List of Kuni no Miyatsuko]] [[ja:国造一覧]] [[sn: failed]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]] [[Category:Kofun period]] [[Category:Kuni no miyatsuko]] [[Category:Titles and Positions in Shintō]] [[Category:Asuka period]] [[en:Kuni no miyatsuko]] [[es:Kuni no miyatsuko]] [[it:Kuni no miyatsuko]] [[ko:국조 (일본)]] [[Category:Pages with simple english wikipedia interwikis]]Kuni no miyatsuko]] [[vi:Kuni no miyatsuko]] [[zh:國造]]

Seihen,” “Various Genealogies,” etc. Since these are of low credibility and do not appear in other reliable sources, it is believed these Kuni no Miyatsuko did not actually exist. {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;font-size:85%" align="left" !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Ritsuryō Province !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" colspan="2" | Name of Kuni no Miyatsuko !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | First Kuni no Miyatsuko
(Period of Appointment) !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Clan (the bracketed term is [[:en:Kabane|Kabane]]) !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Domain !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Notes |- !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" | Notation !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" | Reading |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:Tōkaidō (region)|Tōkaidō (region)]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] | '''{{ill|Shimada Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|嶋田国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimada Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'''
(Owari no Kuni Shimada Kuni no Miyatsuko) || しまだ || Nakaotomi no Koage
(No details on establishment) || Possibly the Shimada clan? (Omuraji) || Southern Owari Province || Possibly linked to the Shimada Omuraji of the Ta clan. Nakaotomi no Koage is said to be the ancestor of the Niwa Agatanushi. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shimōsa Province|Shimōsa Province]] | '''{{ill|Fusa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|布佐国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fusa Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || ふさ || {{ill|Ame no Tomi no mikoto|ja|天富命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Tomi no mikoto|qq=|1=Ame-no-Tomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q24899653}}
(Emperor Jinmu period) || The Imbe (Inbe) clan (Kubi) || Western Shimōsa Province || According to the tradition of {{ill|Takeuchi Shrine (Hyōgo)|ja|竹内神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeuchi Shrine (Hyōgo)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 竹内神社 (我孫子市)|1=Takeuchi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q97218316}}. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:Tōsandō|Tōsandō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shinano Province|Shinano Province]] | '''{{ill|Ina Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|伊奈国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ina Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || いな || Hayagoeue-no-mikoto
(No details on establishment) || Unknown || Southern Shinano Province || However, other documents mention {{ill|Shinano Province|ja|科野国|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano Province|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 科野国造|1=Shinano no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11595951}} as having the {{ill|Shinano (Shinano no Kuni) Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|科野国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano (Shinano no Kuni) Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=|1=Shinano no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11595951}}. Hayagoeue-no-mikoto is the progenitor of the Iyo Kuni no Miyatsuko. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shinano Province|Shinano Province]] | '''{{ill|Suwa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|洲羽国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|qq=|1=Suwa-no-kokuzo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q67499361}}''' || すわ || {{ill|Take Ōomi no mikoto|ja|建大臣命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Take Ōomi no mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武国彦命|1=Takakuni no Hikono Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q100453594}}
[[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] || Unknown || Central Shinano Province || In the “[[:en:Kujiki|Sendai Kuji Hongi (Kujihongi)]]” Kuni no Miyatsuko Honki, the mention of a Kuni no Miyatsuko in Suwa is believed to be an error for {{ill|Nasu Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|那須国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nasu Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=|1=Nasu no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11642909}}. All details such as the appointment period, the founding ancestor Take Ōomi no mikoto, or how it was established, come from the forged texts “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” “Aso Family Brief Genealogy,” “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” and “Various Genealogies,” so it is considered certain to be a fictional Kuni no Miyatsuko.Ryōtarō Maeda, “Reconsidering the ‘Shinshi Keizu’ in the ‘Ōhori-bon’ & ‘Aso-ke ryaku keifu’: Reconstructed Suwa Traditions,” in “Studies in Japanese Language and Literature” No.161, August 2023. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shinano Province|Shinano Province]] | '''{{ill|Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|木蘇国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|qq=|1=Kiso no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q85881055}}''' || きそ || Ototekehiko-no-mikoto
(No details on establishment) || Unknown || Southern Shinano Province || References to Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko appear only in the forged “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” “Aso Family Brief Genealogy,” “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” “Various Genealogies,” etc., so it is regarded as certainly fictional.Ryōtarō Maeda, “Reconsidering the ‘Shinshi Keizu’ in the ‘Ōhori-bon’ & ‘Aso-ke ryaku keifu’: Reconstructed Suwa Traditions,” in “Studies in Japanese Language and Literature” No.161, August 2023. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:San'yōdō|Sanyōdō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Aki Province|Aki Province]] | '''{{ill|Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|沼田国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|qq=|1=Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11554571}}''' || ぬた || {{ill|Akinosayatama no mikoto|ja|飽速玉命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akinosayatama no mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} || The Tsukushi clan || Eastern Aki Province || The priestly family of {{ill|Numata Shrine|ja|沼田神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Numata Shrine|qq=|1=Numata Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11554607}} claims descent from the Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko. Akinosayatama no mikoto is the progenitor of the Aki Kuni no Miyatsuko. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:San'indō|San'indō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Izumo Province|Izumo Province]] | '''{{ill|Susa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|須佐国造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || すさ || Bon-nari

(Possibly during Jingo Keiun 1 [767 CE]) || The Dōshima clan (Sukune) || Mutsu Province || Created by merging the various Mutsu Kuni no Miyatsuko. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Dewa Province|Dewa Province]] | '''{{ill|Dewa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|出羽国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dewa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || でわ || (Wadō 5 [712 CE]) || Unknown || Dewa Province || Split off from Mutsu Province and Echigo Province. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:San'indō|San'indō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Mimasaka Province|Mimasaka Province]] | '''{{ill|Mimasaka Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|美作国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimasaka Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || みまさか || (Wadō 6 [713 CE]) || Unknown || Mimasaka Province || Split off from Bizen Province. |} {{-}} === Kuni no Miyatsuko Deemed Not to Have Existed === The following Kuni no Miyatsuko appear in shrine traditions, in the “Suwa Historical Materials” Volume 28 (the “Suwa Shimo-sha Ōhori (Ohoribe) Takei Iwai Kei Zu Ryaku”), or in what are considered forged texts such as the “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” the “{{ill|Aso Family Brief Genealogy|ja|阿蘇家略系図|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aso Family Brief Genealogy|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}},” the “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” “Various Genealogies,” etc. Since these are of low credibility and do not appear in other reliable sources, it is believed these Kuni no Miyatsuko did not actually exist. {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;font-size:85%" align="left" !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Ritsuryō Province !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" colspan="2" | Name of Kuni no Miyatsuko !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | First Kuni no Miyatsuko
(Period of Appointment) !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Clan (the bracketed term is [[:en:Kabane|Kabane]]) !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Domain !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Notes |- !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" | Notation !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" | Reading |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:Tōkaidō (region)|Tōkaidō (region)]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] | '''{{ill|Shimada Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|嶋田国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimada Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'''
(Owari no Kuni Shimada Kuni no Miyatsuko) || しまだ || Nakaotomi no Koage
(No details on establishment) || Possibly the Shimada clan? (Omuraji) || Southern Owari Province || Possibly linked to the Shimada Omuraji of the Ta clan. Nakaotomi no Koage is said to be the ancestor of the Niwa Agatanushi. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shimōsa Province|Shimōsa Province]] | '''{{ill|Fusa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|布佐国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fusa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || ふさ || {{ill|Ame no Tomi no mikoto|ja|天富命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Tomi no mikoto|1=Ame-no-Tomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q24899653}}
(Emperor Jinmu period) || The Imbe (Inbe) clan (Kubi) || Western Shimōsa Province || According to the tradition of {{ill|Takeuchi Shrine (Hyōgo)|ja|竹内神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeuchi Shrine (Hyōgo)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 竹内神社 (我孫子市)|1=Takeuchi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q97218316}}. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:Tōsandō|Tōsandō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shinano Province|Shinano Province]] | '''{{ill|Ina Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|伊奈国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ina Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || いな || Hayagoeue-no-mikoto
(No details on establishment) || Unknown || Southern Shinano Province || However, other documents mention {{ill|Shinano Province|ja|科野国|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano Province|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 科野国造|1=Shinano no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11595951}} as having the {{ill|Shinano (Shinano no Kuni) Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|科野国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano (Shinano no Kuni) Kuni no Miyatsuko|1=Shinano no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11595951}}. Hayagoeue-no-mikoto is the progenitor of the Iyo Kuni no Miyatsuko. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shinano Province|Shinano Province]] | '''{{ill|Suwa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|洲羽国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|1=Suwa-no-kokuzo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q67499361}}''' || すわ || {{ill|Take Ōomi no mikoto|ja|建大臣命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Take Ōomi no mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武国彦命|1=Takakuni no Hikono Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q100453594}}
[[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] || Unknown || Central Shinano Province || In the “[[:en:Kujiki|Sendai Kuji Hongi (Kujihongi)]]” Kuni no Miyatsuko Honki, the mention of a Kuni no Miyatsuko in Suwa is believed to be an error for {{ill|Nasu Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|那須国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nasu Kuni no Miyatsuko|1=Nasu no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11642909}}. All details such as the appointment period, the founding ancestor Take Ōomi no mikoto, or how it was established, come from the forged texts “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” “Aso Family Brief Genealogy,” “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” and “Various Genealogies,” so it is considered certain to be a fictional Kuni no Miyatsuko.Ryōtarō Maeda, “Reconsidering the ‘Shinshi Keizu’ in the ‘Ōhori-bon’ & ‘Aso-ke ryaku keifu’: Reconstructed Suwa Traditions,” in “Studies in Japanese Language and Literature” No.161, August 2023. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shinano Province|Shinano Province]] | '''{{ill|Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|木蘇国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|1=Kiso no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q85881055}}''' || きそ || Ototekehiko-no-mikoto
(No details on establishment) || Unknown || Southern Shinano Province || References to Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko appear only in the forged “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” “Aso Family Brief Genealogy,” “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” “Various Genealogies,” etc., so it is regarded as certainly fictional.Ryōtarō Maeda, “Reconsidering the ‘Shinshi Keizu’ in the ‘Ōhori-bon’ & ‘Aso-ke ryaku keifu’: Reconstructed Suwa Traditions,” in “Studies in Japanese Language and Literature” No.161, August 2023. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:San'yōdō|Sanyōdō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Aki Province|Aki Province]] | '''{{ill|Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|沼田国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|1=Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11554571}}''' || ぬた || {{ill|Akinosayatama no mikoto|ja|飽速玉命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akinosayatama no mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} || The Tsukushi clan || Eastern Aki Province || The priestly family of {{ill|Numata Shrine|ja|沼田神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Numata Shrine|1=Numata Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11554607}} claims descent from the Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko. Akinosayatama no mikoto is the progenitor of the Aki Kuni no Miyatsuko. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:San'indō|San'indō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Izumo Province|Izumo Province]] | '''{{ill|Susa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|須佐国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || すさ || Bon-nari
(Emperor Seimu period) || The Susa clan || Southwestern Izumo Province || The priestly family of {{ill|Susa Shrine (Shimane)|ja|須佐神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susa Shrine (Shimane)|1=Susa Shrine (Shimane)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11664499}} claims descent from the Susa Kuni no Miyatsuko. |} {{-}} '''Kuni no Miyatsuko Ichiran''' (国造一覧) {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 1]] }} [[ja:国造]] [[ja:国造一覧]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]] [[Category:Kofun period]] [[Category:Kuni no miyatsuko]] [[Category:Titles and Positions in Shintō]] [[Category:Asuka period]]

(Possibly during Jingo Keiun 1 [767 CE]) || The Dōshima clan (Sukune) || Mutsu Province || Created by merging the various Mutsu Kuni no Miyatsuko. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Dewa Province|Dewa Province]] | '''{{ill|Dewa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|出羽国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dewa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || でわ || (Wadō 5 [712 CE]) || Unknown || Dewa Province || Split off from Mutsu Province and Echigo Province. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:San'indō|San'indō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Mimasaka Province|Mimasaka Province]] | '''{{ill|Mimasaka Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|美作国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimasaka Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || みまさか || (Wadō 6 [713 CE]) || Unknown || Mimasaka Province || Split off from Bizen Province. |} {{-}} === Kuni no Miyatsuko Deemed Not to Have Existed === The following Kuni no Miyatsuko appear in shrine traditions, in the “Suwa Historical Materials” Volume 28 (the “Suwa Shimo-sha Ōhori (Ohoribe) Takei Iwai Kei Zu Ryaku”), or in what are considered forged texts such as the “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” the “{{ill|Aso Family Brief Genealogy|ja|阿蘇家略系図|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aso Family Brief Genealogy|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}},” the “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” “Various Genealogies,” etc. Since these are of low credibility and do not appear in other reliable sources, it is believed these Kuni no Miyatsuko did not actually exist. {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;font-size:85%" align="left" !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Ritsuryō Province !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" colspan="2" | Name of Kuni no Miyatsuko !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | First Kuni no Miyatsuko
(Period of Appointment) !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Clan (the bracketed term is [[:en:Kabane|Kabane]]) !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Domain !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Notes |- !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" | Notation !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" | Reading |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:Tōkaidō (region)|Tōkaidō (region)]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] | '''{{ill|Shimada Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|嶋田国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimada Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'''
(Owari no Kuni Shimada Kuni no Miyatsuko) || しまだ || Nakaotomi no Koage
(No details on establishment) || Possibly the Shimada clan? (Omuraji) || Southern Owari Province || Possibly linked to the Shimada Omuraji of the Ta clan. Nakaotomi no Koage is said to be the ancestor of the Niwa Agatanushi. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shimōsa Province|Shimōsa Province]] | '''{{ill|Fusa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|布佐国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fusa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || ふさ || {{ill|Ame no Tomi no mikoto|ja|天富命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Tomi no mikoto|1=Ame-no-Tomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q24899653}}
(Emperor Jinmu period) || The Imbe (Inbe) clan (Kubi) || Western Shimōsa Province || According to the tradition of {{ill|Takeuchi Shrine (Hyōgo)|ja|竹内神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeuchi Shrine (Hyōgo)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 竹内神社 (我孫子市)|1=Takeuchi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q97218316}}. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:Tōsandō|Tōsandō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shinano Province|Shinano Province]] | '''{{ill|Ina Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|伊奈国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ina Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || いな || Hayagoeue-no-mikoto
(No details on establishment) || Unknown || Southern Shinano Province || However, other documents mention {{ill|Shinano Province|ja|科野国|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano Province|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 科野国造|1=Shinano no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11595951}} as having the {{ill|Shinano (Shinano no Kuni) Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|科野国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano (Shinano no Kuni) Kuni no Miyatsuko|1=Shinano no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11595951}}. Hayagoeue-no-mikoto is the progenitor of the Iyo Kuni no Miyatsuko. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shinano Province|Shinano Province]] | '''{{ill|Suwa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|洲羽国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|1=Suwa-no-kokuzo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q67499361}}''' || すわ || {{ill|Take Ōomi no mikoto|ja|建大臣命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Take Ōomi no mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武国彦命|1=Takakuni no Hikono Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q100453594}}
[[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] || Unknown || Central Shinano Province || In the “[[:en:Kujiki|Sendai Kuji Hongi (Kujihongi)]]” Kuni no Miyatsuko Honki, the mention of a Kuni no Miyatsuko in Suwa is believed to be an error for {{ill|Nasu Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|那須国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nasu Kuni no Miyatsuko|1=Nasu no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11642909}}. All details such as the appointment period, the founding ancestor Take Ōomi no mikoto, or how it was established, come from the forged texts “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” “Aso Family Brief Genealogy,” “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” and “Various Genealogies,” so it is considered certain to be a fictional Kuni no Miyatsuko.Ryōtarō Maeda, “Reconsidering the ‘Shinshi Keizu’ in the ‘Ōhori-bon’ & ‘Aso-ke ryaku keifu’: Reconstructed Suwa Traditions,” in “Studies in Japanese Language and Literature” No.161, August 2023. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Shinano Province|Shinano Province]] | '''{{ill|Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|木蘇国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|1=Kiso no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q85881055}}''' || きそ || Ototekehiko-no-mikoto
(No details on establishment) || Unknown || Southern Shinano Province || References to Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko appear only in the forged “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” “Aso Family Brief Genealogy,” “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” “Various Genealogies,” etc., so it is regarded as certainly fictional.Ryōtarō Maeda, “Reconsidering the ‘Shinshi Keizu’ in the ‘Ōhori-bon’ & ‘Aso-ke ryaku keifu’: Reconstructed Suwa Traditions,” in “Studies in Japanese Language and Literature” No.161, August 2023. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:San'yōdō|Sanyōdō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Aki Province|Aki Province]] | '''{{ill|Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|沼田国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|1=Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11554571}}''' || ぬた || {{ill|Akinosayatama no mikoto|ja|飽速玉命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akinosayatama no mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} || The Tsukushi clan || Eastern Aki Province || The priestly family of {{ill|Numata Shrine|ja|沼田神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Numata Shrine|1=Numata Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11554607}} claims descent from the Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko. Akinosayatama no mikoto is the progenitor of the Aki Kuni no Miyatsuko. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''[[:en:San'indō|San'indō]]''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| [[:en:Izumo Province|Izumo Province]] | '''{{ill|Susa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|須佐国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || すさ || Bon-nari
(Emperor Seimu period) || The Susa clan || Southwestern Izumo Province || The priestly family of {{ill|Susa Shrine (Shimane)|ja|須佐神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susa Shrine (Shimane)|1=Susa Shrine (Shimane)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11664499}} claims descent from the Susa Kuni no Miyatsuko. |} {{-}} '''Kuni no Miyatsuko Ichiran''' (国造一覧) {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 1]] }} [[ja:国造]] [[ja:国造一覧]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]] [[Category:Kofun period]] [[Category:Kuni no miyatsuko]] [[Category:Titles and Positions in Shintō]] [[Category:Asuka period]]

Seihen,” “Various Genealogies,” etc. Since these are of low credibility and do not appear in other reliable sources, it is believed these Kuni no Miyatsuko did not actually exist. {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;font-size:85%" align="left" !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Ritsuryō Province !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" colspan="2" | Name of Kuni no Miyatsuko !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | First Kuni no Miyatsuko
(Period of Appointment) !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Clan (the bracketed term is {{ill|Kabane|en|Kabane|WD=Q1664099|lt=Kabane}}) !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Domain !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" rowspan="2" | Notes |- !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" | Notation !style="background:#ccccff; white-space:nowrap" | Reading |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''{{ill|Tōkaidō (region)|en|Tōkaidō (region)|WD=Q1196306|lt=Tōkaidō (region)}}''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| {{ill|Owari Province|en|Owari Province|WD=Q514506|lt=Owari Province}} | '''{{ill|Shimada Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|嶋田国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimada Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'''
(Owari no Kuni Shimada Kuni no Miyatsuko) || しまだ || Nakaotomi no Koage
(No details on establishment) || Possibly the Shimada clan? (Omuraji) || Southern Owari Province || Possibly linked to the Shimada Omuraji of the Ta clan. Nakaotomi no Koage is said to be the ancestor of the Niwa Agatanushi. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| {{ill|Shimōsa Province|en|Shimōsa Province|WD=Q1053695|lt=Shimōsa Province}} | '''{{ill|Fusa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|布佐国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fusa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || ふさ || {{ill|Ame no Tomi no mikoto|ja|天富命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Tomi no mikoto|1=Ame-no-Tomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q24899653}}
(Emperor Jinmu period) || The Imbe (Inbe) clan (Kubi) || Western Shimōsa Province || According to the tradition of {{ill|Takeuchi Shrine (Hyōgo)|ja|竹内神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeuchi Shrine (Hyōgo)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 竹内神社 (我孫子市)|1=Takeuchi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q97218316}}. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''{{ill|Tōsandō|en|Tōsandō|WD=Q1334011|lt=Tōsandō}}''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| {{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province|WD=Q289250|lt=Shinano Province}} | '''{{ill|Ina Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|伊奈国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ina Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || いな || Hayagoeue-no-mikoto
(No details on establishment) || Unknown || Southern Shinano Province || However, other documents mention {{ill|Shinano Province|ja|科野国|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano Province|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 科野国造|1=Shinano no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11595951}} as having the {{ill|Shinano (Shinano no Kuni) Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|科野国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano (Shinano no Kuni) Kuni no Miyatsuko|1=Shinano no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11595951}}. Hayagoeue-no-mikoto is the progenitor of the Iyo Kuni no Miyatsuko. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| {{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province|WD=Q289250|lt=Shinano Province}} | '''{{ill|Suwa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|洲羽国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|1=Suwa-no-kokuzo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q67499361}}''' || すわ || {{ill|Take Ōomi no mikoto|ja|建大臣命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Take Ōomi no mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武国彦命|1=Takakuni no Hikono Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q100453594}}
{{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|WD=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū}} || Unknown || Central Shinano Province || In the “{{ill|Kujiki|en|Kujiki|WD=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi (Kujihongi)}}” Kuni no Miyatsuko Honki, the mention of a Kuni no Miyatsuko in Suwa is believed to be an error for {{ill|Nasu Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|那須国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nasu Kuni no Miyatsuko|1=Nasu no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11642909}}. All details such as the appointment period, the founding ancestor Take Ōomi no mikoto, or how it was established, come from the forged texts “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” “Aso Family Brief Genealogy,” “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” and “Various Genealogies,” so it is considered certain to be a fictional Kuni no Miyatsuko.Ryōtarō Maeda, “Reconsidering the ‘Shinshi Keizu’ in the ‘Ōhori-bon’ & ‘Aso-ke ryaku keifu’: Reconstructed Suwa Traditions,” in “Studies in Japanese Language and Literature” No.161, August 2023. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| {{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province|WD=Q289250|lt=Shinano Province}} | '''{{ill|Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|木蘇国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|1=Kiso no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q85881055}}''' || きそ || Ototekehiko-no-mikoto
(No details on establishment) || Unknown || Southern Shinano Province || References to Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko appear only in the forged “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” “Aso Family Brief Genealogy,” “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” “Various Genealogies,” etc., so it is regarded as certainly fictional.Ryōtarō Maeda, “Reconsidering the ‘Shinshi Keizu’ in the ‘Ōhori-bon’ & ‘Aso-ke ryaku keifu’: Reconstructed Suwa Traditions,” in “Studies in Japanese Language and Literature” No.161, August 2023. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''{{ill|San'yōdō|en|San'yōdō|WD=Q1376722|lt=Sanyōdō}}''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| {{ill|Aki Province|en|Aki Province|WD=Q965029|lt=Aki Province}} | '''{{ill|Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|沼田国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|1=Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11554571}}''' || ぬた || {{ill|Akinosayatama no mikoto|ja|飽速玉命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akinosayatama no mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} || The Tsukushi clan || Eastern Aki Province || The priestly family of {{ill|Numata Shrine|ja|沼田神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Numata Shrine|1=Numata Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11554607}} claims descent from the Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko. Akinosayatama no mikoto is the progenitor of the Aki Kuni no Miyatsuko. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''{{ill|San'indō|en|San'indō|WD=Q1323423|lt=San'indō}}''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| {{ill|Izumo Province|en|Izumo Province|WD=Q582846|lt=Izumo Province}} | '''{{ill|Susa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|須佐国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || すさ || Bon-nari

Nakaotomi no Koage is said to be the ancestor of the Niwa Agatanushi. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| {{ill|Shimōsa Province|en|Shimōsa Province|WD=Q1053695|lt=Shimōsa Province}} | '''{{ill|Fusa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|布佐国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fusa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || ふさ || {{ill|Ame no Tomi no mikoto|ja|天富命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Tomi no mikoto|1=Ame-no-Tomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q24899653}}
(Emperor Jinmu period) || The Imbe (Inbe) clan (Kubi) || Western Shimōsa Province || According to the tradition of {{ill|Takeuchi Shrine (Hyōgo)|ja|竹内神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeuchi Shrine (Hyōgo)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 竹内神社 (我孫子市)|1=Takeuchi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q97218316}}. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''{{ill|Tōsandō|en|Tōsandō|WD=Q1334011|lt=Tōsandō}}''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| {{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province|WD=Q289250|lt=Shinano Province}} | '''{{ill|Ina Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|伊奈国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ina Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || いな || Hayagoeue-no-mikoto

Hayagoeue-no-mikoto is the progenitor of the Iyo Kuni no Miyatsuko. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| {{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province|WD=Q289250|lt=Shinano Province}} | '''{{ill|Suwa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|洲羽国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|1=Suwa-no-kokuzo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q67499361}}''' || すわ || {{ill|Take Ōomi no mikoto|ja|建大臣命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Take Ōomi no mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武国彦命|1=Takakuni no Hikono Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q100453594}}
{{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|WD=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū}} || Unknown || Central Shinano Province || In the “{{ill|Kujiki|en|Kujiki|WD=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi (Kujihongi)}}” Kuni no Miyatsuko Honki, the mention of a Kuni no Miyatsuko in Suwa is believed to be an error for {{ill|Nasu Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|那須国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nasu Kuni no Miyatsuko|1=Nasu no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11642909}}. All details such as the appointment period, the founding ancestor Take Ōomi no mikoto, or how it was established, come from the forged texts “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” “Aso Family Brief Genealogy,” “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” and “Various Genealogies,” so it is considered certain to be a fictional Kuni no Miyatsuko.Ryōtarō Maeda, “Reconsidering the ‘Shinshi Keizu’ in the ‘Ōhori-bon’ & ‘Aso-ke ryaku keifu’: Reconstructed Suwa Traditions,” in “Studies in Japanese Language and Literature” No.161, August 2023. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| {{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province|WD=Q289250|lt=Shinano Province}} | '''{{ill|Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|木蘇国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|1=Kiso no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q85881055}}''' || きそ || Ototekehiko-no-mikoto
(No details on establishment) || Unknown || Southern Shinano Province || References to Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko appear only in the forged “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” “Aso Family Brief Genealogy,” “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” “Various Genealogies,” etc., so it is regarded as certainly fictional.Ryōtarō Maeda, “Reconsidering the ‘Shinshi Keizu’ in the ‘Ōhori-bon’ & ‘Aso-ke ryaku keifu’: Reconstructed Suwa Traditions,” in “Studies in Japanese Language and Literature” No.161, August 2023. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''{{ill|San'yōdō|en|San'yōdō|WD=Q1376722|lt=Sanyōdō}}''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| {{ill|Aki Province|en|Aki Province|WD=Q965029|lt=Aki Province}} | '''{{ill|Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|沼田国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|1=Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11554571}}''' || ぬた || {{ill|Akinosayatama no mikoto|ja|飽速玉命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akinosayatama no mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} || The Tsukushi clan || Eastern Aki Province || The priestly family of {{ill|Numata Shrine|ja|沼田神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Numata Shrine|1=Numata Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11554607}} claims descent from the Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko. Akinosayatama no mikoto is the progenitor of the Aki Kuni no Miyatsuko. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''{{ill|San'indō|en|San'indō|WD=Q1323423|lt=San'indō}}''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| {{ill|Izumo Province|en|Izumo Province|WD=Q582846|lt=Izumo Province}} | '''{{ill|Susa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|須佐国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || すさ || Bon-nari

{{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|WD=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū}} || Unknown || Central Shinano Province || In the “{{ill|Kujiki|en|Kujiki|WD=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi (Kujihongi)}}” Kuni no Miyatsuko Honki, the mention of a Kuni no Miyatsuko in Suwa is believed to be an error for {{ill|Nasu Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|那須国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nasu Kuni no Miyatsuko|1=Nasu no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11642909}}. All details such as the appointment period, the founding ancestor Take Ōomi no mikoto, or how it was established, come from the forged texts “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” “Aso Family Brief Genealogy,” “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” and “Various Genealogies,” so it is considered certain to be a fictional Kuni no Miyatsuko.Ryōtarō Maeda, “Reconsidering the ‘Shinshi Keizu’ in the ‘Ōhori-bon’ & ‘Aso-ke ryaku keifu’: Reconstructed Suwa Traditions,” in “Studies in Japanese Language and Literature” No.161, August 2023. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| {{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province|WD=Q289250|lt=Shinano Province}} | '''{{ill|Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|木蘇国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|1=Kiso no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q85881055}}''' || きそ || Ototekehiko-no-mikoto

Seihen,” “Various Genealogies,” etc., so it is regarded as certainly fictional.Ryōtarō Maeda, “Reconsidering the ‘Shinshi Keizu’ in the ‘Ōhori-bon’ & ‘Aso-ke ryaku keifu’: Reconstructed Suwa Traditions,” in “Studies in Japanese Language and Literature” No.161, August 2023. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''{{ill|San'yōdō|en|San'yōdō|WD=Q1376722|lt=Sanyōdō}}''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| {{ill|Aki Province|en|Aki Province|WD=Q965029|lt=Aki Province}} | '''{{ill|Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|沼田国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|1=Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11554571}}''' || ぬた || {{ill|Akinosayatama no mikoto|ja|飽速玉命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akinosayatama no mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} || The Tsukushi clan || Eastern Aki Province || The priestly family of {{ill|Numata Shrine|ja|沼田神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Numata Shrine|1=Numata Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11554607}} claims descent from the Numata Kuni no Miyatsuko. All details such as the appointment period, the founding ancestor Take Ōomi no mikoto, or how it was established, come from the forged texts “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” “Aso Family Brief Genealogy,” “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” and “Various Genealogies,” so it is considered certain to be a fictional Kuni no Miyatsuko.Ryōtarō Maeda, “Reconsidering the ‘Shinshi Keizu’ in the ‘Ōhori-bon’ & ‘Aso-ke ryaku keifu’: Reconstructed Suwa Traditions,” in “Studies in Japanese Language and Literature” No.161, August 2023. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| {{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province|WD=Q289250|lt=Shinano Province}} | '''{{ill|Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|木蘇国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|1=Kiso no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q85881055}}''' || きそ || Ototekehiko-no-mikoto

All details such as the appointment period, the founding ancestor Take Ōomi no mikoto, or how it was established, come from the forged texts “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” “Aso Family Brief Genealogy,” “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” and “Various Genealogies,” so it is considered certain to be a fictional Kuni no Miyatsuko.Ryōtarō Maeda, “Reconsidering the ‘Shinshi Keizu’ in the ‘Ōhori-bon’ & ‘Aso-ke ryaku keifu’: Reconstructed Suwa Traditions,” in “Studies in Japanese Language and Literature” No.161, August 2023. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| {{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province|WD=Q289250|lt=Shinano Province|1=Shinano Province}} | '''{{ill|Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|木蘇国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|1=Kiso no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q85881055}}''' || きそ || Ototekehiko-no-mikoto

(Owari no Kuni Shimada Kuni no Miyatsuko) || しまだ || Nakaotomi no Koage
(No details on establishment) || Possibly the Shimada clan? (Omuraji) || Southern Owari Province || Possibly linked to the Shimada Omuraji of the Ta clan. Nakaotomi no Koage is said to be the ancestor of the Niwa Agatanushi. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| {{ill|Shimōsa Province|en|Shimōsa Province|qid=Q1053695|lt=Shimōsa Province|1=Shimōsa Province}} | '''{{ill|Fusa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|布佐国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fusa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || ふさ || {{ill|Ame no Tomi no mikoto|ja|天富命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Tomi no mikoto|1=Amatomi no Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q24899653}}
(Emperor Jinmu period) || The Imbe (Inbe) clan (Kubi) || Western Shimōsa Province || According to the tradition of {{ill|Takeuchi Shrine (Hyōgo)|ja|竹内神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeuchi Shrine (Hyōgo)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 竹内神社 (我孫子市)|1=Takeuchi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q97218316}}. |- |colspan="7" style="background-color:#C0C0C0"|'''{{ill|Tōsandō|en|Tōsandō|qid=Q1334011|lt=Tōsandō|1=Tōsandō}}''' |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| {{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province|qid=Q289250|lt=Shinano Province|1=Shinano Province}} | '''{{ill|Ina Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|伊奈国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ina Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' || いな || Hayagoeue-no-mikoto
(No details on establishment) || Unknown || Southern Shinano Province || However, other documents mention {{ill|Shinano Province|ja|科野国|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano Province|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 科野国造|1=Shinano no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11595951}} as having the {{ill|Shinano (Shinano no Kuni) Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|科野国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano (Shinano no Kuni) Kuni no Miyatsuko|1=Shinano no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11595951}}. Hayagoeue-no-mikoto is the progenitor of the Iyo Kuni no Miyatsuko. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| {{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province|qid=Q289250|lt=Shinano Province|1=Shinano Province}} | '''{{ill|Suwa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|洲羽国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|1=Suwa-no-kokuzo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q67499361}}''' || すわ || {{ill|Take Ōomi no mikoto|ja|建大臣命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Take Ōomi no mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武国彦命|1=Takakuni no Hikono Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q100453594}}
{{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|qid=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū|1=Empress Jingū}} || Unknown || Central Shinano Province || In the “{{ill|Kujiki|en|Kujiki|qid=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi (Kujihongi)|1=Kujiki}}” Kuni no Miyatsuko Honki, the mention of a Kuni no Miyatsuko in Suwa is believed to be an error for {{ill|Nasu Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|那須国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nasu Kuni no Miyatsuko|1=Nasu no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11642909}}. All details such as the appointment period, the founding ancestor Take Ōomi no mikoto, or how it was established, come from the forged texts “{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Kuji Hongi Taiseikyō|qq=}},” “Aso Family Brief Genealogy,” “Shūho Suwa-shi Keizu. Seihen,” and “Various Genealogies,” so it is considered certain to be a fictional Kuni no Miyatsuko.Ryōtarō Maeda, “Reconsidering the ‘Shinshi Keizu’ in the ‘Ōhori-bon’ & ‘Aso-ke ryaku keifu’: Reconstructed Suwa Traditions,” in “Studies in Japanese Language and Literature” No.161, August 2023. |- | align="center" style="background:#E3E3FF"| {{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province|qid=Q289250|lt=Shinano Province|1=Shinano Province}} | '''{{ill|Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|ja|木蘇国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiso Kuni no Miyatsuko (myth)|1=Kiso no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q85881055}}''' || きそ || Ototekehiko-no-mikoto
